roster.name: EJP-RD Resource Metadata Model (resource-metadata-schema)
roster.description: Project-specific metadata model and schema (version 1.0) for describing rare-disease resources (patient registries, biobanks, catalogs, datasets, data services, guidelines). Provides module documentation, Excel/templates, RDF/Turtle examples, ShEx validation shapes, and guidance for onboarding to the EJP Virtual Platform.

roster.name: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) — Version 2
roster.description: W3C DCAT v2 used as the base vocabulary for describing datasets/catalogs/resources. The seed material explains DCAT2 concepts and how the EJP model maps to and extends DCAT (including guidance and examples).

roster.name: EJP‑RD DCAT extension (vocabulary)
roster.description: The repository documents a custom DCAT2 extension that adds EJP-specific classes/properties (e.g., ejp:Biobank, ejp:PatientRegistry, ejp:Guideline) and mapping annotations; includes diagrams and links to the extension repo.

roster.name: ShEx (Shape Expressions)
roster.description: ShEx shapes provided for validation of the EJP metadata modules (patientRegistry, biobank, catalog, dataset, distribution, dataservice, etc.), with example ShEx code and visual figures — guidance on validating metadata instances.

roster.name: RDF / Turtle serialization (Semantic Web RDF)
roster.description: Guidance and example RDF/Turtle serializations for implementing the metadata model in RDF, with recommended use of RDF as an implementation format and concrete Turtle examples for each module.

roster.name: Dublin Core / DCMI Metadata Terms (DCT)
roster.description: Dublin Core terms (dct:) are used throughout the model (e.g., dct:title, dct:publisher, dct:spatial); the docs show how to use these properties within the EJP metadata modules and examples.

roster.name: FOAF (Friend Of A Friend) vocabulary
roster.description: FOAF classes/properties (foaf:Organisation, foaf:page, foaf:Agent) are used in the examples and shapes to represent organisations/publishers and contact pages; the docs show usage in module examples.
